gaps.sentence: Such ___ the chaos at the airport that hundreds slept on the terminal floor.
gaps.explanation: 'Such was the chaos that…' — emphatic fronting of 'such' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: So difficult ___ the exam that half the candidates failed.
gaps.explanation: So difficult was the exam that… — inversion for emphasis.

gaps.sentence: Only later ___ we realise what he had done.
gaps.explanation: 'Only later did we realise' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: Among the guests ___ the ambassador and her staff.
gaps.hint: fronted 'among' — verb agrees with later subject
gaps.explanation: Among the guests were the ambassador and her staff — verb before subject.

gaps.sentence: Only after the interview ___ I realise how nervous I had been.
gaps.explanation: Only after X did I realise… — inversion.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the chances of success be improved by patience.
gaps.explanation: Little will the chances be improved… — inversion with future.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than problems arose.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive with inversion: had … been signed.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the play cancelled, but the theatre was closed as well.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the play cancelled' — inverted passive.
